claimant_lives_in_uk.description: Whether the claimant lives in the UK.

children.description: A list of children the claimant is claiming for.

lives_with_claimant.description: Whether the child lives with the claimant.

in_approved_education.description: Whether the child is in approved education or training (e.g. A-levels, GCSEs, NVQ up to level 3). Only relevant for children aged 16-19.

in_extension_period.description: Whether the child (aged 16 or 17) has left education and registered with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed forces (qualifying for a 20-week extension).

upkeep_per_week.description: The amount in £ per week the claimant contributes towards the child's upkeep (food, clothes, pocket money, etc.). Only relevant if the child does not live with the claimant.

another_claimant_has_priority.description: Whether another person who also lives with the child has priority for claiming Child Benefit.

another_claimant_lives_with_child.description: Whether someone who lives with the child is already claiming Child Benefit for them.

care_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in local authority care.

care_home_24h_per_week.description: Whether the child spends at least 24 hours per week at home while in local authority care.

hospital_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in hospital or residential accommodation.

claimant_spends_on_child.description: Whether the claimant regularly spends money on the child (e.g. food, clothes, books) while the child is in hospital or residential accommodation.

is_fostered.description: Whether the child is fostered by the claimant.

council_pays_for_child.description: Whether the local council pays towards the child's accommodation or maintenance.

works_24_plus_hours.description: Whether the child works 24 or more hours per week in paid employment.

started_apprenticeship_in_england.description: Whether the child has started an apprenticeship in England.

receives_qualifying_benefits.description: Whether the child receives qualifying benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance.

conversation.text:
Hello! I'd be happy to help you determine if you're eligible for Child Benefit. To assess your eligibility, I need to ask you some questions.

Let's start with: **Do you have any children, and if so, how many children are you inquiring about?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Hi, yes I have one child - my son Alex. He's 6 years old. I wanted to check if I can claim Child Benefit for him?

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information! You have a 6-year-old son named Alex. Let me ask you a few questions to determine your eligibility.

**Are you responsible for Alex? That is, do you live with him and are you the person who looks after him (for example, providing food, clothing, and ensuring he goes to school)?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, Alex doesn't live with me actually. He lives with his mum. I don't really contribute financially at the moment either.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for clarifying that. Since Alex lives with his mum and you don't contribute financially or care for him on a day-to-day basis, this is important information.

Just to confirm: **Is there anyone else you are responsible for, or is Alex the only child you're inquiring about for Child Benefit?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Alex is the only child I'm inquiring about, yes.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for confirming. I have enough information to assess your eligibility for Child Benefit for Alex.

Based on what you've told me:
- Alex is your 6-year-old son
- He does not live with you
- You are not responsible for him (his mum looks after him)
- You don't contribute financially to his care

Child Benefit is paid to the person who is responsible for the child - meaning the person the child lives with and who looks after them day-to-day. Since Alex lives with his mum and she is the one looking after him, she would be the person eligible to claim Child Benefit for Alex, not you.

conversation.text:
**Unfortunately, you are not eligible to claim Child Benefit for Alex.**

The key rule is that Child Benefit is only paid to the person who is responsible for the child - this means the person the child lives with and who looks after them on a day-to-day basis. Since Alex lives with his mother and she is the one caring for him, she would be the eligible person to claim Child Benefit for Alex, not you.

If your circumstances change in the future and Alex comes to live with you and you become responsible for his care, you would then be able to claim Child Benefit for him at that time.

Since the claimant is not responsible for Alex, they are ineligible to claim Child Benefit for him.
